title.narrative: Strengthening Access to GBV Prevention and Response Services for Conflict Affected Communities in Bama and Konduga LGAs, Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn northeast Nigeria, women and girls face heightened risks of GBV due to displacement, poverty, and insecurity. A 2024 Gender Analysis by CARE and RESILAC*2 partners (ACF, REBHI, NEEM and NADA) revealed high levels of intimate partner violence, early/forced marriage and harassment in public spaces, with adolescent girls most at risk. Limited access to timely health and psychosocial support further deepens vulnerabilities, especially during the lean season.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis project, ‘Strengthening Access to GBV Prevention and Response Services for Conflict Affected Communities in Bama and Konduga LGAs, Borno State’, will directly reach 6,229 people across the two LGAs. This includes women: 2,048, girls: 2,045, men: 1,096, and boys: 1,040. Out of these, 933 persons with disabilities (307 women, 306 girls, 164 men, and 156 boys) will be intentionally targeted to ensure inclusivity.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe response component will renovate and operationalize a Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS) in Bama to deliver confidential case management and referral services. Focused psychosocial support will be provided to 150 vulnerable individuals. Coordination with the Ministry of Women Affairs and SEMA will ensure alignment with state GBV frameworks.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo meet dignity needs, 20 vulnerable women and girls in Konduga will be trained at REBHI’s dignity kit production center on reusable sanitary pads, himar, and kit assembly, and supported with starter kits for sustainability. They will produce 790 dignity kits 640 distributed to vulnerable women and girls (96 for PLWD) and 150 prepositioned as a flood contingency stock. Consumables will be procured to ensure continuity, with post distribution monitoring to assess satisfaction.ltbrgtFor prevention and risk reduction, 12 GBV Champions (6 male, 6 female) will be trained on GBV, PSEA, and disability inclusion to lead door-to-door sensitization, reaching 5,097 people (1,547 women, 1,500 girls, 1,050 men, 1,000 boys, including 764 PLWD). In addition, 12 SAA facilitators will run four 12 weeks cycles (160 participants total, including 16 PLWD) to challenge harmful gender norms and strengthen community accountability. Safety audits will identify GBV risks in public spaces for community led solutions.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAccountability will be strengthened by establishing safe complaint and feedback mechanisms (helpdesks, boxes, hotlines, focal persons). Communities will be sensitized on their use, ensuring confidential and timely resolution. Monthly monitoring of case management, sensitization, SAA sessions, and safety audits will ensure interventions remain responsive and inclusive.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtOverall, the project strengthens access to survivor centered services while building resilience and community ownership in Bama and Konduga, directly contributing to NHF objectives of reducing vulnerabilities, safeguarding dignity, and promoting resilience during the lean season.ltbrgtlt/pgt
